tools.name: screen_mark
tools.description:
Screen a brand name against the live trademark registers. Free, no account.

    Returns every mark near it with a similarity tier, plus which registers were
    checked. This is the first thing to run when someone asks 'is my name taken'.

description.name: my_conflicts
description.description: Everything currently near the names this user watches.

description.name: my_deadlines
my_watches
description.description: The names this user is watching.

description.name: company_file
description.description:
A holder's WHOLE book across every office. Founder and up.

    Corporate identity from PermID (organisation, HQ, PermID) comes with
    `company.attribution`, its CC BY 4.0 credit.

description.name: follow_filer
description.description:
Follow an adversary — every filing they make, anywhere. Studio and up.

    Different from watching a name: this catches what they do NEXT, which is usually
    a different name in a class the user doesn't hold.

description.name: watch_mark
description.description:
Start watching a brand name: new filings near it show up as conflicts.

    Optionally takes Nice classes as a comma-separated list ('9,42'); blank watches
    every class.

description.name: dismiss_conflict
description.description:
Clear one hit as not-a-threat. Reversible — it moves to the Cleared list.

    Takes `jurisdiction` and `app_no` exactly as they appear on a conflict in the
    user's conflict list. A cleared hit, such as an unrelated business or the user's
    own filing, stops being surfaced.

description.name: filer_activity
description.description: What the filers this user follows have filed lately. Studio and up.

description.name: run_investigation
description.description:
Research a trademark holder on the open web and return a cited dossier: who they
    really are (an operating company, a shell, a known squatter), their notable
    trademark activity or disputes, and any red flags. Signed-in.

    Spends one credit — included credits first, then purchased ones. A f

description.name: get_credit_balance
description.description:
How many credits this user can spend and what each paid tool costs, in credits.
    Free to call.

    `remaining` is what can be spent now: `monthly_left` (included with their plan,
    resets each month) plus `topup_balance` (bought, never expires). `prices` is
    credits per call, by tool.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "check_names" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
